schemes.label: Partita IVA

provenance.sourceText: «2. La fattura contiene le seguenti indicazioni: [...] d) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cedente o prestatore».

schemes.notes: DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 21, comma 2, lettera d). Read directly at normattiva.it (https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21!vig=, plain HTTP response headed "vigente al 13/09/2026", curl with a browser User-Agent, no JS rendering needed), 2026-09-13. This binds the SELLER only ("cedente o prestatore") and carries no carve-out anywhere in comma 2 — a flat-rate/forfettario trader still holds and must state a Partita IVA. Cross-checked against the simplified-invoice regime at art. 21-bis, comma 1, lettera d) (same method/date, https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21bis!vig=): the seller's Partita IVA is NOT among the elements a simplified invoice (<=EUR100, raised to <=EUR400) may omit. Also cross-checked against the FatturaPA technical specification's own introduction, which restates the DPR 633/1972 list including "numero di partita IVA del cedente/prestatore" with no qualifier. For the SELLER this is genuinely unconditional — no VAT-regime carve-out exists. `required` is nonetheless set to `false` here, and this is the one deliberate departure from simply transcribing the seller's own unconditional rule: this catalog's ONLY axis is `appliesTo` (COMPANY/INDIVIDUAL/BOTH — the PARTY's own record type), and `resolveRequiredIdentifiers` takes no notion of transactional role at all. The exact same per-country array is read by `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` (always `partyType: "COMPANY"`, for the ACTIVE company about to issue invoices — i.e. always the SELLER in this product's outbound flow) AND by `client-upsert.tsx` (partyType taken from the CLIENT's own record type — i.e. the BUYER of that company's invoices). Setting `required: true` here would therefore ALSO become a hard block on saving an Italian, company-type CLIENT record — confirmed by reading client-upsert.tsx's `onSubmit` (a `required` scheme with an empty value calls `form.setError(...)` and `return`s, refusing to save) — but the BUYER-side rule is genuinely CONDITIONAL (DPR 633/1972 art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) — see this file's own LEGAL_ID entry below for the quote and the reasoning), not unconditional like the seller's. There is no per-role `required` in this schema, and the DB itself only allows one row per (countryCode, scheme) — `CountryIdentifierRequirement`'s unique key is `countryCode_scheme` — so a second "VAT" fact scoped to the buyer could not even coexist with this one; the seed would just overwrite it. `required: false` at country level is the same discipline this catalog already applies in fr.json/pt.json when a rule that IS mandatory for most sellers depends on a variable the catalog does not carry per party (there, the seller's own VAT regime; here, the party's ROLE in the transaction) — never a UI default, an explicit and documented choice. `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` is similarly a simplification: an individual professional/sole trader acting as a business (an INDIVIDUAL record in this app) also holds and must state a Partita IVA when acting as a taxable person under this same lettera d) — but this choice is moot for the seller path specifically, because `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` always query `partyType: "COMPANY"` regardless of the active company's real legal form, so this fact is shown there unconditionally either way; it only affects whether an INDIVIDUAL-typed CLIENT also sees this field (optionally, since `required` is false here). FORMAT: the commonly-cited 11-digit numeric format for Partita IVA was NOT found in either DPR 633/1972 art. 21 or the FatturaPA Specifiche tecniche v1.4 (whose own `IdCodice` field states only a generic 28-character ceiling shared with foreign identifiers) — no `pattern` is declared here for that reason, the same discipline pt.json already applies to its own undeclared NIF/NIPC pattern.

schemes.label: Codice Fiscale

provenance.resolutionNote: Italian law does not always ask a buyer for the same document. A business buyer gives their VAT number (their Italian Partita IVA, or — if they are a business established elsewhere in the EU — their own country's VAT number instead). A buyer who is NOT acting as a business — typically a private individual — gives their Italian tax code (Codice Fiscale) instead of a VAT number. Right now this app has no way to tell those two situations apart for a given client: it only records whether a client is filed as a "Company" or an "Individual", and that is not the same thing as whether the client is acting as a VAT-registered business — an individual can run a business (and would then need to give a VAT number, not a tax code), and some companies are not VAT-registered (and would then need to give a tax code instead). Until a client record can say which of the two applies, this app cannot safely make either the VAT number or the Codice Fiscale mandatory here: doing so would sometimes ask a private individual for a business VAT number they will never have, or let a business through with neither number recorded. What would settle this: letting a client record say whether it is acting as a VAT-registered business, separately from whether it is filed as a Company or an Individual — once that exists, the correct one of the two identifiers can be safely required.

schemes.notes: DPR 633/1972, art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) (same page/method/date as the VAT entry above, 2026-09-13): the lettering repeats in the retrieved text — an "e)" covers the buyer's name/domicile and a first "f)" restates it, then a further "f)" (quoted here, semicolon-separated within the same point) states the actual number rule — quoted exactly as normattiva.it renders it, not tidied: «f) ditta, denominazione o ragione sociale, nome e cognome, residenza o domicilio del soggetto cessionario o committente, del rappresentante fiscale nonché ubicazione della stabile organizzazione per i soggetti non residenti; f) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cessionario o committente ovvero, in caso di soggetto passivo stabilito in un altro Stato membro dell'Unione europea, numero di identificazione IVA attribuito dallo Stato membro di stabilimento; nel caso in cui il cessionario o committente residente o domiciliato nel territorio dello Stato non agisce nell'esercizio d'impresa, arte o professione, codice fiscale;» Precisely: an Italian-established taxable-person buyer gives Partita IVA; a taxable person established in another EU Member State gives THEIR OWN state's VAT id, not an Italian Partita IVA; a buyer resident/domiciled in Italy who does NOT act in the exercise of a business, art or profession gives Codice Fiscale instead. Cross-validated by a second, independent primary source, the FatturaPA technical specification's own `CessionarioCommittente` block, which states the same alternative structurally: «IdFiscaleIVA (la valorizzazione di questi elementi è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento CodiceFiscale; in altri termini, possono non essere valorizzati se è valorizzato l'elemento CodiceFiscale; [...]) [...] CodiceFiscale: la valorizzazione di questo elemento è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento IdFiscaleIVA (può non essere valorizzato se è valorizzato l'elemento IdFiscaleIVA); consente l'inserimento del numero di codice fiscale del cessionario/committente.» (same PDF/URL as this file's VAT entry's own IT-3-equivalent citation — see this file's top-level `notes`). Also cross-validated by the simplified-invoice regime, art. 21-bis comma 1 lettera e): a simplified invoice can reduce the buyer's identification to "il solo codice fiscale o il numero di partita IVA" for an Italy-established buyer, the same CF/VAT alternative. `appliesTo: 'BOTH'` and `required: false` are both deliberate: BOTH because either a COMPANY-record or an INDIVIDUAL-record buyer can legally need either identifier depending on taxable-person status, not on record type (an INDIVIDUAL freelancer needs Partita IVA exactly like a COMPANY; a COMPANY-record entity that is not a taxable person would need Codice Fiscale exactly like a private INDIVIDUAL) — `appliesTo` cannot express that finer axis, so BOTH is the least wrong choice, not a claim that record type decides anything here. `required: false` because the rule is a genuine either/or conditioned on taxable-person status, which this catalog does not track per party (see this fact's own `resolutionNote`) — setting it `true` under either scheme name would demand a document some lawful buyers do not have. `provenance.kind` is `unverified` here NOT because the underlying law is in doubt (it is fully quoted above, read directly at normattiva.it) but because a fact this well-established in law, yet not safely enforceable by this product (the deciding variable, taxable-person status, exists nowhere in this app's data model) is recorded as `unverified` with a `resolutionNote` naming what the product would need, rather than graded `legal` with a `required` value that cannot honestly reflect a role-dependent rule. FORMAT: Codice Fiscale length IS established as 11-16 alphanumeric characters (Specifiche tecniche v1.4, §3.3.1, `DatiAnagraficiCedenteType`: «CodiceFiscale (Rif. par. 3.2): formato alfanumerico; lunghezza compresa tra 11 e 16 caratteri.», repeated identically for `RappresentanteFiscale` and `CessionarioCommittente`) — no `pattern` is declared on this fact regardless, by the same all-or-nothing discipline de.json's own VAT entry already uses (an unsourced claim elsewhere in the same fact keeps the whole fact from being promoted); if this fact is ever promoted, `^.{11,16}$` is the primary-sourced pattern to use.

schemes.label: Codice Univoco Ufficio (IPA)

provenance.sourceText: «CodiceDestinatario: identifica il soggetto al quale è destinata la fattura; - nei casi di fattura destinata ad una Pubblica Amministrazione il suo valore, di 6 caratteri, deve corrispondere a quello presente nel campo Codice Ufficio riportato nella rubrica "Indice PA" (WWW.INDICEPA.GOV.IT).»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. Line wraps closed and typographic quotes normalised in the quotation above; wording unchanged. appliesTo COMPANY: only a Pubblica Amministrazione holds a Codice Ufficio in IndicePA, and this product records a government client as `Client.kind === 'GOVERNMENT'` on a COMPANY-shaped record -- there is no INDIVIDUAL-shaped government body. required false: the scheme is effectively mandatory, but only for the GOVERNMENT subset, an axis `appliesTo` cannot express (it distinguishes party TYPE, not `kind`). `b2g-routing/data/it.json` already enforces the real requirement for that subset at send time. Requiring it here would block saving an ordinary Italian business client that will never be a PA. pattern: 6 alphanumeric characters, from "il suo valore, di 6 caratteri" above, cross-checked against the same document's length table at par. 3.2 ("lunghezza che va da 6 a 7 caratteri" -- 6 is the PA branch, 7 the non-PA one). Case-insensitive because `fatturapa-provider.ts` uppercases before emitting CodiceDestinatario.

schemes.label: Codice Destinatario (SdI)
schemes.helpText: 7-character code the Sistema di Interscambio assigns on request ('Richiesta codici destinatario B2B' on fatturapa.gov.it) to a non-PA recipient with an accredited receiving channel. Needed so a domestic B2B/private invoice routes to the right mailbox instead of falling back to a placeholder.

provenance.sourceText: «CodiceDestinatario: identifica il soggetto al quale è destinata la fattura; [...] - nei casi di fattura destinata ad un soggetto diverso da Pubblica Amministrazione il suo valore, di 7 caratteri, deve corrispondere a: uno dei codici che il Sistema di Interscambio attribuisce ai soggetti, con canale accreditato in ricezione, che ne abbiano fatto richiesta attraverso la funzione "Richiesta codici destinatario B2B" presente sul sito WWW.FATTURAPA.GOV.IT; [...]»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Same document, fetch and date as the IT_PA_CODE fact above. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. schemes.label: PEC (Posta Elettronica Certificata)
schemes.helpText: Certified email address used as the SdI delivery channel when the recipient has no Codice Destinatario (SdI) on file. Only used for a non-PA recipient.

provenance.sourceText: «PECDestinatario: indirizzo di Posta Elettronica Certificata al quale viene recapitata la fattura; viene valorizzato nei soli casi di destinatario diverso da Pubblica Amministrazione, qualora il destinatario utilizzi il canale PEC per ricevere le fatture. Può essere valorizzato solo se il valore di CodiceDestinatario è uguale a '0000000'.» Same par. 1.1, on the CodiceDestinatario branch itself: «'0000000', nei casi di fattura destinata ad un soggetto che riceve tramite PEC e questa sia indicata nel campo PECDestinatario;»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Same document, fetch and date as the IT_PA_CODE fact above. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. Line wraps closed and typographic quotes normalised in the quotation above; wording unchanged. appliesTo BOTH and required false for the same reasons as IT_SDI: the text gates on a non-PA recipient without restricting to businesses, and this is the SECOND fallback, reached only when no SdI code exists. NO pattern on purpose: the specification's length table at par. 3.2 states only "formato alfanumerico; lunghezza che va da 7 a 256 caratteri" -- a length range, not an email grammar. Declaring a generic address regex would be a formal claim no primary source here supports, which this catalog's provenance discipline forbids.

identifiers.notes:
Italy, five schemes. VAT and LEGAL_ID are both `required: false` because this catalog's `appliesTo` axis is party TYPE, while Italy's buyer-side rule (DPR 633/1972 art. 21 comma 2 lettera f) turns on whether the buyer is a taxable person -- a distinction the schema does not carry, and which the DB's one-row-per-(country, scheme) shape cannot express as two role-scoped facts. Requiring either would hard-block a lawful client record. Each fact's own notes state the asymmetry in full.

IT_PA_CODE, IT_SDI and PEC are declared here because `formats/national/fatturapa-provider.ts` reads all three off the client to route FormatoTrasmissione and CodiceDestinatario, and this catalog is the only thing that makes a field for them exist: `client-upsert.tsx` renders one input per scheme declared for the party's country, keying its data-cy off `req.scheme` with no allowlist. While they were undeclared, a domestic Italian B2B client could not have its SdI code entered anywhere and fell through to CodiceDestinatario 'XXXXXXX' -- the value this same specification reserves for a recipient "non residente, non stabilito, non identificato in Italia". A domestic invoice announced to SdI as a foreign one.

`b2g-routing/data/it.json` separately declares IT_PA_CODE as mandatory for GOVERNMENT clients. The two are not duplicates: this catalog makes the field EXIST on any Italian record, that one makes it REQUIRED for that subset at send time.

provenance.sourceText: Art. 16 Aliquote dell'imposta ((L'aliquota dell'imposta è stabilita nella misura del ventidue per cento della base imponibile dell'operazione)). ((171))

rates.notes: DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 16, comma 1 (the version currently in force until 2026-12-31, art.versione=11 on normattiva.it). Read directly on 2026-09-13 on https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633 — the body of the article is loaded by the site's internal endpoint (/atto/caricaArticolo?...), itself a same-origin, server-generated HTML response (no JavaScript executed), reached with curl carrying a session cookie and the art.versione/idGruppo/idArticolo parameters read off the summary page's own markup. The double parentheses ((...)) in the citation are normattiva.it's convention for flagging text amended by a later law — footnote (171), also read directly, concerns a 2016 drafting tweak (L. n. 208/2015, art. 1, comma 963) and not the value of the rate, which dates from 2013 (raised from 21% to 22%). SCHEDULED REPEAL: the entirety of art. 16 and of Tabella A of DPR 633/1972 is repealed as of 2027-01-01 by D.Lgs. 19 gennaio 2026, n. 10 (the new Testo Unico IVA, TUIVA — official title read directly on normattiva.it, meta-description: « Testo unico delle disposizioni legislative in materia di imposta sul valore aggiunto. (26G00022) »). The act's own changelog (the vediAggiornamentiAllAtto endpoint, read directly on 2026-09-13) confirms: « ha disposto (con l'art. 170, comma 1, lettera a)) l'abrogazione dell'art. 16. [...] ha disposto (con l'art. 170, comma 1, lettera a)) l'abrogazione della tabella A. » (the « [...] » elides an intermediate line, also a repeal, targeting art. 13 — unrelated to the rates). The new art. 34 of the TUIVA (read directly, same method as art. 16 above) CARRIES OVER THE SAME FIGURES identically: « ART. 34 Aliquote dell'imposta ( articolo 16 decreto del Presidente della Repubblica 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633 ; articolo 43, comma 5, decreto-legge 30 agosto 1993, n. 331 [...] ) 1. L'aliquota dell'imposta è stabilita nella misura del 22 per cento della base imponibile dell'operazione. 2. L'aliquota è ridotta al 4, al 5 e al 10 per cento per le operazioni che hanno per oggetto i beni e i servizi elencati, rispettivamente, nella parte II, nella parte III e nella parte IV della tabella A allegata al presente testo unico, salvo il disposto dell'articolo 133. » — only the CITATION changes (art. 16 → TUIVA art. 34; Tabella A parte II/II-bis/III → parte II/III/IV), not the percentage. This catalog does not model temporality (no validFrom/validTo in schema.ts): the citation above therefore stays DPR 633/1972 for as long as the latter remains in force (until 2026-12-31), and it is up to whoever next touches this file after 2027-01-01 to re-point the citation to the TUIVA — nothing in the schema will flag this automatically.

vatRates.notes: Italy (2026-09-13, zero-rate entries added 2026-09-17). Six rates, all 'legal', SOURCED FROM THE PRIMARY TEXT via normattiva.it (the official portal of the Italian State's consolidated law): DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 16 + Tabella A — 22% (ordinary, comma 1), 10% (parte III), 5% (parte II-bis), 4% (parte II, comma 2). NO LITERAL '0%' RATE EXISTS: the research searched the entire consolidated text of DPR 633/1972 for the literal phrase « aliquota … zero » / « aliquota del 0 » and found NONE. Two DISTINCT non-taxation regimes exist instead, not interchangeable, and are now BOTH modeled (it-esente, it-non-imponibile — see each entry's own note): 'esenti' transactions (art. 10 — exempt, no deduction right, category EXEMPT, FatturaPA Natura N4) and 'non imponibili' transactions (art. 8, export supplies — non-taxable, deduction right preserved, category ZERO, FatturaPA Natura N3). This schema's separate ZERO and EXEMPT categories are exactly what makes distinguishing the two possible without conflating them — the 2026-09-13 research's own conclusion ('no entry until the schema can tell them apart, or two distinct EXEMPT entries') undersold what schema.ts already offered: it never needed a schema change, only READING art. 8's and art. 10's own category correctly. Without either entry, a purely domestic exempt/non-taxable invoice line (an art. 10 medical service, an art. 8 export) had NO way to leave this catalog's dropdown other than a foreign-looking custom value the 'select' field kind would reject outright — this is what actually blocked a normal, entirely domestic Italian invoice from ever being issued. TABELLA A, PARTE I (« PRODOTTI AGRICOLI E ITTICI ») IS NOT MODELED EITHER: art. 16, comma 2 expressly excludes it (« salvo il disposto dell'articolo 34 ») — it is not a percentage a seller freely chooses but a flat-rate compensation mechanism for agricultural/fishing producers, set by a separate ministerial decree, not read by this research. 2027-01-01 REPEAL: see each entry's own note above (D.Lgs. 19 gennaio 2026, n. 10, new TUIVA — arts. 8/10/16/34 all repealed and re-enacted with the same substance, only the citation changes; confirmed directly against normattiva.it's own post-repeal text for arts. 8 and 10 too, not merely inferred from art. 16's own note). rule.rateDateRule: The exchange rate of the day the operation was carried out, or, absent that, the day the invoice was issued (DPR 633/1972 art. 13 c.4). This codebase has no separate 'day the operation was carried out' distinct from the invoice's own issue date, so the rate is resolved for the document's own issue date, the second (fallback) branch the statute itself names. ECB is used as the rate source: the statute itself does not name a provider, but the EU VAT directive's own art. 91§2 backstop (the last ECB-published rate) is the reference every member state must accept absent its own rule, and Italy's own statute states no different provider, see `notes`.

provenance.sourceText: DPR 633/1972, art. 13, comma 4: "Ai fini della determinazione della base imponibile i corrispettivi dovuti e le spese e gli oneri sostenuti in valuta estera sono computati secondo il cambio del giorno di effettuazione dell'operazione o, in mancanza di tale indicazione nella fattura, del giorno di emissione della fattura." Art. 21, comma 2, lettera l): the invoice must carry "aliquota, ammontare dell'imposta e dell'imponibile con arrotondamento al centesimo di euro": i.e. both the taxable amount and the VAT amount, in euros, regardless of the invoice's own currency.

rule.notes: **DPR 633/1972 is repealed 2027-01-01**, replaced by a new consolidated VAT text ("Testo Unico dell'IVA", D.Lgs. 10/2026, decree dated 19/01/2026, published 30/01/2026 in Gazzetta Ufficiale Serie Generale n. 24, Supplemento ordinario n. 4; entry into force confirmed by the new text's own art. 171). Research carried out for this issue (2026-09-28, WebSearch/WebFetch against gazzettaufficiale.it, normattiva.it, and professional tax-law commentary; Gazzetta Ufficiale and Normattiva both only rendered the table of contents/preamble through automated fetch, never the substantive article bodies) found NO source suggesting either rule (euro-denominated taxable amount + VAT on the invoice; exchange rate = day of operation, else day of invoice) is being dropped or weakened: every source describes the recodification as 'un riordino organico' / 'senza introdurre generalmente una riforma sostanziale del tributo', a reorganisation, not a substantive reform. **The rule is judged to SURVIVE the recodification.** The new article numbers are reported by secondary commentary only, NOT verified against the primary Normattiva text directly, so they are named here as a caveat rather than a second legal citation: a professional concordance table (Nord Ovest Consulting, nord-ovest.it, a client briefing PDF) maps old art. 21+21-bis (invoice content, including the comma 2 lett. l) euro-rounding rule) to new art. 72+73 of the Testo Unico; a secondary summary of commercialistatelematico.com (itself not directly fetchable, HTTP 403) reports old art. 13 (taxable base, including the comma 4 exchange-rate rule) becoming new art. 27, paraphrasing the same day-of-operation/day-of-invoice/ECB-option rule as carried over unchanged. Brocardi.it's own 'testo-unico-iva' pages are a trap confirmed during this research: despite the URL, they still mirror the OLD DPR 633/1972 text under the OLD numbering, not the 2027 recodification. Do not cite them as the new TU. This catalog entry keeps citing DPR 633/1972 by its current, verbatim, in-force numbering (art. 13 c.4 / art. 21 c.2 lett. l) since that is what governs every invoice issued before 2027-01-01; whoever revisits this file after that date must re-verify the new art. 27/72 numbering against Normattiva's actual rendered article text (not yet obtainable through automated fetch as of this check) before citing it as 'legal' provenance in its own right.

facts.notes: Penalty (art. 1, comma 6, D.Lgs. 127/2015, Normattiva consolidated text, same page as sourceText above, checked 2026-09-13): an invoice issued, between subjects resident or established in Italy, by a means other than the one in comma 3, is deemed NOT ISSUED - « In caso di emissione di fattura, tra soggetti residenti o stabiliti nel territorio dello Stato, con modalità diverse da quelle previste dal comma 3, la fattura si intende non emessa e si applicano le sanzioni previste dall'articolo 6 del decreto legislativo 18 dicembre 1997, n. 471. » The effective date of the general mandate (2019-01-01, above) comes from the official Normattiva annotation attached to the same article (« AGGIORNAMENTO (3) »: L. 27 December 2017, n. 205, art. 1 comma 916 - applicable to invoices issued from 1 January 2019), not from the text of comma 3 itself. The forfetario regime is NO LONGER exempt today, contrary to what a maintainer might assume: the exemption was removed in two stages by D.L. 30 April 2022, n. 36 (official Normattiva annotation « AGGIORNAMENTO (19) », same page, checked 2026-09-13) - « Il D.L. 30 aprile 2022, n. 36 ha disposto (con l'art. 18, comma 3) che la modifica di cui al comma 3 del presente articolo "si applica a partire dal 1° luglio 2022 per i soggetti che nell'anno precedente abbiano conseguito ricavi ovvero percepito compensi, ragguagliati ad anno, superiori a euro 25.000, e a partire dal 1° gennaio 2024 per i restanti soggetti. [...]" » - 1 July 2022 for forfettari who had exceeded €25,000 of turnover (ragguagliato ad anno) the previous year, 1 January 2024 for everyone else. The ONLY exemptions that remain today (Agenzia delle Entrate, official guidance page, banner « dichiarazione precompilata 2026 », checked 2026-09-13) are two categories already exempt from invoicing ALTOGETHER (not a regime specific to electronic invoicing), plus a separate PROHIBITION for reasons of sensitive data: « Sono obbligati ad emettere la fattura elettronica tutti i soggetti, residenti o stabiliti in Italia, titolari di partita Iva che effettuano operazioni nei confronti di soggetti residenti o stabiliti in Italia. Sono esonerati dall'obbligo di fatturazione elettronica i soggetti già in precedenza dispensati per legge dall'emissione della fattura (anche cartacea) quali, ad esempio, i "piccoli produttori agricoli" (di cui all'art. 34, comma 6, del Dpr n. 633/1972) e i soggetti che hanno richiesto la dispensa dagli adempimenti di fatturazione ai sensi dell'art. 36-bis del Dpr n. 633/72 relativamente alle operazioni esenti. Vige il divieto di emissione di fattura elettronica via SdI per le prestazioni sanitarie verso consumatori finali, effettuate dagli operatori sanitari, in virtù dei dati particolarmente sensibili contenuti in tali fatture. » None of these three situations (the two exemptions, the healthcare prohibition) is modeled by this fact today. But it understands exactly ONE narrowing, `parties: 'domestic'`, and these three Italian situations are not it: they turn on a taxpayer's STATUS or on a document's subject matter, neither of which this catalog carries. field.label: Supply type
field.helpText: Whether this line is a delivery of goods or a supply of services — it decides how a cross-border sale is taxed. Goods sold to a consumer in another EU member state are an intra-Community distance sale, taxed where they arrive once your EU-wide distance sales pass EUR 10 000 in a calendar year (Directive 2006/112/EC art. 33(a) and art. 59c); the same sale as a service stays taxable here (art. 45). Optional: a line that declares nothing is treated as a supply of services.

countryFields.notes: Italy's FIRST field overlay — the SAME `supplyType` line subfield France's own `fr.json` already adds, in the same shape: kind 'select', values GOODS/SERVICES, OPTIONAL, added to `invoice.lines` rather than to the trunk `descriptors/invoice.descriptor.ts`, which stays country-blind. WHY THE FIELD IS IDENTICAL IN ALL FIVE COUNTRIES RATHER THAN A PER-COUNTRY VARIANT: what reads it — `tax/resolve-invoice-tax.ts`, feeding `tax/tax-engine.ts#determineLineTax` — branches on the goods/services distinction of Directive 2006/112/EC (arts. 32, 33(a) and 59c for an intra-Community distance sale of goods, art. 45 for a service), which binds every member state identically; the same reasoning `tax/types.ts`'s own `DistanceSalesRegime` states for art. 59c ('art. 59c applies identically in all of them'). Italy's transposition defines the two in the directive's own terms — « Costituiscono cessioni di beni gli atti a titolo oneroso che importano trasferimento della proprietà ovvero costituzione o trasferimento di diritti reali di godimento su beni di ogni genere » (DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 2, primo comma) against « Costituiscono prestazioni di servizi le prestazioni verso corrispettivo dipendenti da contratti d'opera, appalto, trasporto, mandato, spedizione, agenzia, mediazione, deposito e in genere da obbligazioni di fare, di non fare e di permettere quale ne sia la fonte » (same decree, art. 3, primo comma). Read in raw text on 2026-09-21 at normattiva.it (https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:presidente.repubblica:decreto:1972-10-26;633 , act updated to 11/08/2026); the article bodies load from a session-bound endpoint, so a bare fetch of the act URL returns the navigation shell only — carry the session cookie from that first request. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED FROM FRANCE: the French overlay's own `helpText` names BT-23 (« cadre de facturation »), which is a FRENCH obligation — `formats/semantic/business-process.ts#resolveFrenchBusinessProcessCode` derives that code only for a seller whose country has an active BT-23 rule in `content-requirements/`, and France is the only country with one — so an Italian seller declaring a supply type changes the exported document not at all; it changes the TAX determination, which is what this file's own help text names instead. NO RETROACTIVE EFFECT ON STORED DOCUMENTS: the field is OPTIONAL and nothing back-fills it. `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a line's raw `supplyType` to GOODS/SERVICES and treats anything else — including absent — as SERVICES, emitting a named warning; that fallback is untouched here, so every invoice stored before this file existed resolves exactly as it did before, and only a line a user explicitly marks as goods reaches the distance-sales branch. DIGITAL IS NOT OFFERED, on purpose: `tax/types.ts`'s own `SupplyType` has a third value, but `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a stored value to GOODS/SERVICES only, so a 'DIGITAL' option would be silently discarded on the way in — offering it would need that narrowing widened first, for all five countries including France.

The OBLIGATION itself (mandatory e-invoicing toward the PA) rests on DM 55/2013 (« di cui all'Allegato A del DM 55/2013 », cited BY this official document itself, in its own page header) and its enabling act, L. 244/2007 art. 1 commi 209-214 — neither text could be reached DIRECTLY by this task (gazzettaufficiale.it and normattiva.it rendered only navigation shells to a plain request); the citation above therefore rests on the OFFICIAL technical document that referenced them, not on the decrees themselves. `transportId: "sdi"` and `formatSyntax: "fatturapa"` are BOTH channels/formats ALREADY IMPLEMENTED in this repository (`transports/sdi-transport.ts`, `formats/national/fatturapa-provider.ts`) — unlike FR/DE above, an Italian invoice to a government client can therefore actually go out, once the company has connected the SdI channel. KNOWN GAP, NOT FIXED BY THIS TASK (declared scope: the B2G routing RULE, not the format builder itself): `fatturapa-provider.ts` hard-codes `versione: 'FPR12'` (« fattura verso privati ») for EVERY invoice, including one to a `GOVERNMENT` client — the document above reveals that a PA invoice should carry `FPA12` (« fattura verso PA »), not `FPR12`. This task does NOT modify `fatturapa-provider.ts` (outside its declared scope: the routing table, not the XML builder) — the rule above only guarantees the Codice Univoco (IPA) is actually REQUIRED on the client before sending, never that it is correctly injected into an XML that would otherwise carry the wrong `FormatoTrasmissione`.
